units.function: Limits Docker build context by excluding Git, local state, dependencies, logs and caches.
units.dependencyDirection: Constrains the root Docker build input.
units.keyDataModels: No business data; excludes local `.paperclip` and database state.
units.lifecycle: Applied before Docker stages and therefore part of secret/data leakage prevention.
units.testAssessment: A Docker dependency-stage check exists, but build-context negative assertions are not comprehensive.
units.designRationale: Reduce image context, cache invalidation and accidental local-data inclusion.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS must keep credentials, production data and local execution state out of images.
units.companyOsFit: Directly relevant as a pattern, with Company OS-specific paths and secret checks.
units.responsibilityConflict: Leaked local state could expose evidence, credentials or responsibility records.

units.function: Documents local database, server/UI and authentication/signing environment variables.
units.dependencyDirection: Feeds server configuration conventions; contains development placeholder secrets.
units.keyDataModels: Connection URL and secret-bearing configuration keys.
units.lifecycle: Copied by operators for development; unsafe values must never become production defaults.
units.testAssessment: Configuration parsing is tested elsewhere, but the example itself can drift and has no schema-generation link.
units.designRationale: Minimize local startup friction.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs profile-specific, validated configuration without real credentials.
units.companyOsFit: The discoverability fits; Company OS should generate examples from typed config and reject placeholder secrets in production.
units.responsibilityConflict: A signing secret affects action authority and must be deployment-owned, rotated and audience-bound.

units.function: Excludes dependencies, builds, environment files, runtime state, reports, tool scratch and worktrees.
units.dependencyDirection: Repository hygiene only; several negations keep audit scripts tracked.
units.keyDataModels: Names local state classes that must not enter source control.
units.lifecycle: Protects normal development, but cannot replace secret scanning or data-classification gates.
units.testAssessment: Git status and secret scanners detect some mistakes; ignored files are inherently less visible to repository checks.
units.designRationale: Separate source from generated, runtime and developer-specific state.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS also needs explicit source/runtime/data separation.
units.companyOsFit: Use the principle, not the exact paths.
units.responsibilityConflict: Formal evidence must not be treated as disposable ignored scratch; production evidence belongs in governed storage.

units.function: Normalizes multiple contributor identities for Git statistics.
units.dependencyDirection: Affects contributor reporting, not product runtime.
units.keyDataModels: Contributor identity aliases.
units.lifecycle: Maintained as author addresses change.
units.testAssessment: No dedicated test; Git tooling consumes it directly.
units.designRationale: Avoid double-counting contributors in release and maintenance metrics.
units.companyOsProblem: Open-source governance also needs accurate contributor provenance.
units.companyOsFit: Useful repository practice but not reusable product code.
units.responsibilityConflict: Git authorship is not organizational approval or accountable-human identity.

units.function: Enables automatic peer installation.
units.dependencyDirection: Changes dependency resolution for the whole workspace.
units.keyDataModels: No business data.
units.lifecycle: Applied at install time and can change the resolved graph when peer ranges change.
units.testAssessment: Frozen lockfile checks constrain normal CI, but standalone excluded plugins are separate.
units.designRationale: Reduce manual peer dependency friction in a plugin-heavy monorepo.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs deterministic extension dependency resolution.
units.companyOsFit: Convenient but implicit; prefer explicit peer ownership and frozen lock validation.
units.responsibilityConflict: None directly; implicit dependency installation is a supply-chain concern.

units.function: Grants MIT rights to Paperclip source subject to copyright and permission-notice preservation.
units.dependencyDirection: Applies to first-party Paperclip code unless a nested dependency or asset states separate terms.
units.keyDataModels: No runtime data; copyright and license text are provenance records.
units.lifecycle: Any substantial copied portion must retain the notice in Company OS distribution and provenance.
units.testAssessment: License presence is mechanically checked by Company OS research governance; per-asset and dependency licenses still require their own review.
units.designRationale: Permit broad reuse without warranty while preserving attribution.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs legal selective reuse and auditable notices.
units.companyOsFit: Compatible with selective legal reuse, but does not grant Paperclip trademarks, logos or third-party asset rights.
units.responsibilityConflict: None.

units.function: Root command graph, toolchain pin, dependency overrides and patched-dependency ownership.
units.dependencyDirection: Orchestrates all workspaces through pnpm; does not contain a runtime domain boundary.
units.keyDataModels: No business records; release package map, workspace scripts and dependency resolution are operational metadata.
units.lifecycle: Install links the Plugin SDK; build/typecheck/test fan out; database, release, smoke, visual and eval commands have separate lanes.
units.testAssessment: Many scripts have focused tests and CI callers, but the root has no single proof that every declared command is exercised.
units.designRationale: Centralize a large monorepo while preserving package-local builds and split slow or environment-sensitive test lanes.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS also needs reproducible workspace orchestration, split quality gates and explicit release commands.
units.companyOsFit: The lane separation fits; the very large command surface and upstream-local patches would be excessive at current Company OS scale.
units.responsibilityConflict: None directly; scripts must not become an alternate path around production responsibility gates.

units.function: Carries local changes to `acpx` process/session behavior and `embedded-postgres` locale/environment propagation.
units.dependencyDirection: Root package resolution injects these patches into third-party distributions; product runtime behavior therefore depends on local fork deltas.
units.keyDataModels: ACPX session options/process callbacks and embedded Postgres process environment, not Company OS domain records.
units.lifecycle: Every dependency upgrade must rebase and retest patches; `acpx` has a packaging test while embedded Postgres behavior has package-level tests.
units.testAssessment: There is explicit ACPX patch packaging coverage, but patches still enlarge the long-term maintenance and supply-chain review surface.
units.designRationale: Fill missing upstream hooks for process supervision, environment transfer, Windows parsing and portable embedded Postgres startup.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS will face child-process supervision, platform quoting and local database portability problems.
units.companyOsFit: The problems matter, but copying compiled distribution patches would be brittle; use supported upstream APIs or owned adapters.
units.responsibilityConflict: Agent spawn hooks and environment transfer are security-critical and must bind to an authorized work/run lease.

units.function: Pins the root workspace dependency graph and records patched dependency resolution.
units.dependencyDirection: Covers included pnpm workspaces, not deliberately excluded standalone sandbox providers.
units.keyDataModels: Package versions, integrity hashes, peer snapshots and importer dependency edges.
units.lifecycle: Updated by dependency changes and a dedicated refresh workflow; consumed by frozen installs and release images.
units.testAssessment: PR scripts validate lock changes and production audit was run; vulnerability results are time- and advisory-database-specific.
units.designRationale: Reproducible monorepo installs with explicit dependency overrides.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs reproducible builds, SBOM input and vulnerability gates.
units.companyOsFit: Required pattern, but no Paperclip version or importer should be copied.
units.responsibilityConflict: None directly; compromised dependencies can bypass all application responsibility semantics.

units.function: Defines workspace membership and deliberately excludes sandbox providers and one orchestration smoke fixture from the root lock graph.
units.dependencyDirection: Packages join the root graph by glob; excluded packages install independently and can drift from the canonical lock.
units.keyDataModels: No business data; workspace membership is build provenance.
units.lifecycle: Root install covers core packages while standalone plugins own separate installation and lock behavior.
units.testAssessment: Release and plugin smoke tests cover some exclusions; there is no universal cross-lock compatibility proof.
units.designRationale: Avoid root lockfile churn from provider-specific plugin dependencies.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS will need extension isolation without losing reproducibility or SBOM coverage.
units.companyOsFit: Useful separation, but production extensions should still require pinned lockfiles and signed provenance.
units.responsibilityConflict: Independent plugin installs can enlarge the supply-chain boundary and must not inherit human authority.

units.function: Shared strict TypeScript compiler defaults for NodeNext ES2023 packages.
units.dependencyDirection: Inherited outward by package configs; `skipLibCheck` trusts dependency declarations.
units.keyDataModels: No runtime data.
units.lifecycle: Affects source, declarations and maps for every inheriting workspace.
units.testAssessment: Compilation exercises it broadly; compiler-option intent is not separately contract-tested.
units.designRationale: Keep module and declaration behavior consistent across many packages.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs strict common settings and deterministic module boundaries.
units.companyOsFit: Mostly aligned; Company OS should keep strict mode and add explicit noUncheckedIndexedAccess/exact optional policy only when migration cost is understood.
units.responsibilityConflict: None.

units.function: TypeScript project-reference graph for shared, database, adapters, server, UI and CLI.
units.dependencyDirection: Declares intended build order, but references a missing `packages/adapters/droid-local` path and omits some present packages.
units.keyDataModels: No business data; project references encode compile-time architecture.
units.lifecycle: Consumed by root and package typecheck/build commands; drift can create untyped build gaps.
units.testAssessment: A dedicated `typecheck:build-gaps` script compensates for incomplete ordinary reference coverage.
units.designRationale: Use incremental package builds while tolerating a rapidly changing workspace inventory.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs a compile graph that exactly matches its product package graph.
units.companyOsFit: Project references fit, but Company OS should reject missing or unreferenced first-party packages automatically.
units.responsibilityConflict: None.

units.function: Aggregates 18 package/application Vitest projects.
units.dependencyDirection: Root test orchestration invokes package-local configs; sandbox-provider and several plugin workspaces are outside this list.
units.keyDataModels: No business data; test-project membership is quality metadata.
units.lifecycle: Stable runner scripts shard general and serialized projects for CI reliability.
units.testAssessment: Broad but not exhaustive project membership; excluded packages rely on separate scripts or their own CI paths.
units.designRationale: Bound memory, ordering and environmental conflicts in a large suite.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs deterministic unit/integration/E2E separation and visibility into excluded projects.
units.companyOsFit: The sharding pattern fits later scale; a manifest completeness guard should precede it.
units.responsibilityConflict: None.

units.function: Shared runtime substrate for local, SSH and sandbox execution: process lifecycle, ACPX, sessions, workspace transfer, managed runtimes, callback bridge, env shaping, redaction, skills, billing and transcript types.
units.dependencyDirection: All first-party Agent adapters depend inward on this package; it depends on `acpx` and `picocolors`, while also carrying server, CLI and UI-facing types. Server core imports it directly.
units.keyDataModels: AdapterAgent, AdapterRuntime, AdapterExecutionContext/Result, execution targets, session codec/compaction, runtime services, skill snapshots, transcript entries and callback bridge requests.
units.lifecycle: Prepare workspace/runtime → shape environment and credentials → spawn or resume process/session → stream logs/events → collect usage/result → restore workspace → terminate/clean up. Remote and sandbox paths add transfer and bridge leases.
units.testAssessment: 22 focused tests cover process, SSH, sandbox confinement, sync/restore, MCP isolation, callback authorization, redaction and session behavior. Large `server-utils.ts` and ~3,800-line ACPX executor still concentrate many coupled branches and integration assumptions.
units.designRationale: Normalize heterogeneous CLI/ACP runtimes and prevent each provider adapter from reimplementing transport, process and workspace safety.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs equal Connector lifecycle, remote/local execution nodes, fencing, cancellation, timeout, evidence, workspace/data egress and secret-safe runtime proof.
units.companyOsFit: Many invariants are valuable, but the contract mixes Paperclip issue/heartbeat vocabulary, raw auth token injection, provider sessions, UI transcript types and transport implementation. It is not a neutral Company OS Connector SDK.
units.responsibilityConflict: ExecutionContext carries authority as an optional raw `authToken`, while permission bypass and tool actions are adapter concerns; Company OS requires action-digest approval and accountable-human responsibility before any capability lease is issued.

units.function: Documents and tests the no-remote-git persistence contract for adapters.
units.dependencyDirection: Constrains adapters, adapter-utils, server and CLI; static CI rejects unapproved `git push` paths.
units.keyDataModels: Execution workspace, transported copy, remote URL metadata and finalize status.
units.lifecycle: Local worktree is authoritative across runs; remote copies sync out and back, and failed restoration blocks dependent work.
units.testAssessment: A fixture test proves remote-only commits return without any configured remote; a static source scan enforces the policy with reasoned exceptions.
units.designRationale: Avoid hidden dependence on credentials, remotes or branch publication for cross-run durability.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS execution nodes need an explicit durable-state owner and must distinguish work persistence from external publication.
units.companyOsFit: Strongly aligned. Company OS should generalize it to an Artifact/WorkspacePort and require publication as a separately approved action.
units.responsibilityConflict: Implicit `git push` would be an unapproved external side effect; the ban supports Company OS responsibility semantics.

units.function: Runs Claude Code through CLI or ACP, with model/quota discovery, config/skill materialization, local/remote execution and transcript parsing.
units.dependencyDirection: Depends on adapter-utils and Claude ACP; imported directly by server and UI, so provider details cross backend/frontend boundaries.
units.keyDataModels: Provider config, ACP session, model profile, quota windows, skill snapshot and execution result.
units.lifecycle: Auto-select ACP or CLI → materialize config/skills → probe auth/model → execute/resume → parse output/usage → preserve session and workspace.
units.testAssessment: Eight focused tests cover ACP fallback, remote execution, permissions, parsing, config and probes. Credential/config materialization and host-provider calls remain sensitive integration surfaces.
units.designRationale: Offer one adapter despite two execution engines and several Claude authentication modes.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs vendor-neutral engine negotiation and runtime health without losing provider-specific capabilities.
units.companyOsFit: Engine fallback and remote permission narrowing are useful patterns; direct code is coupled to Paperclip env, prompt and session semantics.
units.responsibilityConflict: `dangerouslySkipPermissions` defaults true and local confinement is off by default. Company OS must never treat provider bypass flags as organizational approval.

units.function: Runs Codex by CLI or ACP with model profiles, output/process inactivity monitoring, isolated homes, device login and identity-keyed credential cache/copyback.
units.dependencyDirection: Depends on adapter-utils and Codex ACP; server and UI import provider constants, schemas, parsers and execution hooks.
units.keyDataModels: Codex session, managed CODEX_HOME, subscription account identity, cached credential version, device-login transcript and runtime config.
units.lifecycle: Resolve engine/home/auth precedence → optionally vend only a newer same-identity credential → execute with activity monitor → parse usage/session → merge credential updates under lock → restore workspace.
units.testAssessment: 26 tests are the strongest adapter suite and cover auth precedence, path/symlink safety, copyback races, device-login parsing, activity monitoring, remote execution and output parsing.
units.designRationale: Keep long-lived subscription credentials usable across isolated runs without cross-company or cross-account credential substitution.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS had not yet fully specified identity-anchored credential refresh/copyback, silent-process liveness or auth-format migration.
units.companyOsFit: These are important requirements to add to Secret/Execution ports; implementation remains Codex/Paperclip filesystem and auth-format specific.
units.responsibilityConflict: The adapter exposes a bypass-approvals/sandbox default and must not equate CLI device identity with accountable enterprise human authority.

units.function: Invokes durable Cursor Cloud Agents through the vendor SDK and maps Paperclip heartbeats to remote runs.
units.dependencyDirection: Direct vendor SDK dependency; server passes issue/run context and a minted Paperclip token into the remote environment.
units.keyDataModels: Repository/runtime identity, durable Cursor agent session, remote run attachment, vendor API key and execution result.
units.lifecycle: Validate vendor config → create or reattach durable remote agent → inject scoped run environment → wait/poll remote run → preserve session identity.
units.testAssessment: Four tests cover execution, session identity and UI parsing; actual vendor failure, cancellation, billing and data-residency paths need live-contract tests.
units.designRationale: Let the vendor own remote code execution while Paperclip retains task state.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs external managed-runtime connectors with explicit residency, cancellation, timeout, evidence and exit semantics.
units.companyOsFit: The ownership split is useful, but vendor session and token injection must stay inside a Connector adapter and local execution node.
units.responsibilityConflict: A remote vendor run can act on a repository; Company OS must bind the exact repository/data/action scope to a responsibility contract and approval digest.

units.function: Runs Cursor Agent CLI locally or remotely with session resume, stream parsing, skills and trust controls.
units.dependencyDirection: Depends on adapter-utils; vendor CLI installation uses an unpinned remote installer and execution results flow into server/UI parsers.
units.keyDataModels: Cursor session/cwd identity, model profile, stream events and remote command.
units.lifecycle: Resolve command/model → transport workspace if remote → execute/resume session → parse stream → restore workspace.
units.testAssessment: Four tests cover local/remote execution and command selection; installer provenance, credential isolation and cancellation receive limited direct coverage.
units.designRationale: Normalize Cursor's local CLI despite the lack of a registry-distributed installer artifact.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs an install provenance policy for execution-node tooling.
units.companyOsFit: Runtime shape is ordinary Connector adapter work; unpinned `curl | bash` is not acceptable for enterprise production.
units.responsibilityConflict: Tool installation and repository writes are separate high-risk actions and cannot inherit work approval automatically.

units.function: Runs Gemini CLI through ACP or CLI with fallback, session parsing, remote execution and skill materialization.
units.dependencyDirection: Depends on adapter-utils; provider-specific config and transcript modules are imported by server and UI.
units.keyDataModels: Gemini ACP/CLI session, provider config, skill snapshot and execution result.
units.lifecycle: Check ACP prerequisites/version → choose engine → stage config/skills/workspace → execute → parse/resume → restore.
units.testAssessment: Six focused tests cover ACP, fallback, remote behavior, parsing and UI config; vendor auth and quota contracts are mostly probe-driven.
units.designRationale: Mask Gemini CLI version and ACP capability variation behind one adapter.
units.companyOsProblem: Connector negotiation must express optional engine versions and deterministic fallback without changing work identity.
units.companyOsFit: Capability negotiation is useful; implementation and session details remain vendor-specific.
units.responsibilityConflict: Fallback must not silently change sandbox or permission guarantees; Company OS must attest the actual engine and confinement used.

units.function: Runs Grok CLI as a single-turn/session-resumable coding Agent and normalizes turn boundaries and transcripts.
units.dependencyDirection: Depends on adapter-utils; workspace skills and provider stream formats flow to server/UI.
units.keyDataModels: Session ID/cwd, streaming turn boundary, tool/result transcript and runtime skill set.
units.lifecycle: Stage project skills → execute or resume → recognize provider turn boundaries → capture result/session → restore workspace.
units.testAssessment: Seven tests emphasize parsers, turn boundaries, config and environment probes; remote and security coverage is thinner than Codex/Claude.
units.designRationale: Prevent provider stream quirks from leaking into core run state.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs connector conformance tests for progress/result ordering and duplicate terminal events.
units.companyOsFit: Parser lessons are relevant, but no generic code should be copied into core.
units.responsibilityConflict: Provider turn completion is not Company OS work completion; evidence and responsibility projections must decide terminal state.

units.function: Provides local and gateway Hermes adapters plus an Agent-facing task-bridge skill that can call Paperclip REST APIs.
units.dependencyDirection: Local execution depends on adapter-utils; gateway and task bridge add outbound HTTP and Paperclip credential semantics within the same distributable package.
units.keyDataModels: Hermes session, provider/model config, gateway transport, task-bridge scope and API key.
units.lifecycle: Detect local configuration or gateway → execute/resume → parse output; independently, the task bridge reads a scoped API key and mutates tasks.
units.testAssessment: Eight tests cover execution spawn, command/model resolution, prompt rendering, bridge scope and UI parsing. Gateway and internet-facing bridge require stronger adversarial/E2E coverage.
units.designRationale: Support Hermes as both a managed employee and an external entry point into task management.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs to separate execution connectors from inbound delegated-control connectors and give each distinct scopes/audiences.
units.companyOsFit: The package demonstrates the danger of combining these roles. Company OS should define separate Connector profiles and credentials.
units.responsibilityConflict: Agent-originated task mutation can create goals or delegation; it must identify the human sponsor and cannot use a normal execution credential.

units.function: Compatibility/re-export shim exposing the gateway implementation from the Hermes package.
units.dependencyDirection: Depends entirely on `@paperclipai/hermes-paperclip-adapter`; contains no independent runtime logic.
units.keyDataModels: None beyond re-exported Hermes gateway types.
units.lifecycle: Built and published as a separate package wrapper; behavior changes whenever the underlying Hermes package changes.
units.testAssessment: No package-local tests; confidence is indirect through the underlying package.
units.designRationale: Preserve package naming/compatibility while consolidating implementation.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS may eventually need deprecation shims for Connector packages.
units.companyOsFit: No current need and no reusable implementation.
units.responsibilityConflict: None beyond the underlying gateway.

units.function: Connects to OpenClaw over WebSocket, performs gateway/device authentication, optional auto-pairing, session routing and wake/result normalization.
units.dependencyDirection: Depends on adapter-utils and `ws`; adapter config may contain shared tokens/passwords and defaults to broad `operator.admin` scopes.
units.keyDataModels: Gateway connection challenge, device identity, shared auth, scopes, session key strategy, wait request and normalized runtime service reports.
units.lifecycle: Resolve credentials/device → open/challenge/connect → optionally approve pairing → send Agent request → wait/stream → normalize result → close or retain session route.
units.testAssessment: Two large tests cover execution protocol and UI config, but broad scopes, first-connect auto-approval and reconnect/cancel races warrant dedicated security/property tests.
units.designRationale: Integrate a remote Agent runtime whose native protocol has its own pairing and session semantics.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs connector bootstrap/pairing, capability attenuation, revocation, reconnect and remote identity proof.
units.companyOsFit: The problem is important; the Paperclip/OpenClaw wire implementation must remain adapter-specific and credentials must be secret references.
units.responsibilityConflict: Default `operator.admin` and automatic pairing are incompatible with least privilege unless a human approves the exact connector enrollment and capability set.

units.function: Runs OpenCode CLI with multi-provider model discovery, session resume, runtime config/skills and optional remote sandbox execution.
units.dependencyDirection: Depends on adapter-utils; installer executes an unpinned remote script and server expands credential placeholders into provider config.
units.keyDataModels: Provider/model ID, session/cwd, generated opencode config, skill set and execution result.
units.lifecycle: Install/probe → discover model → generate runtime config with resolved refs → execute/resume → parse result → restore workspace.
units.testAssessment: Seven tests cover execution, remote path, models, parsing and runtime config; installer integrity and generated-secret cleanup are not equivalent to a full threat-model test.
units.designRationale: Support a provider-agnostic Agent CLI and avoid installing several unused architecture binaries.
units.companyOsProblem: Execution nodes need signed/pinned tool acquisition and ephemeral secret materialization with destruction proof.
units.companyOsFit: Multi-provider selection belongs above the adapter, but unverified `curl | bash`, permission bypass default and secret-bearing generated files conflict with enterprise defaults.
units.responsibilityConflict: External-directory permission defaults true; generated provider credentials can outlive the approved action unless lease cleanup is proven.

units.function: Runs Pi coding Agent with provider/model discovery, sessions, skills and generated provider runtime configuration.
units.dependencyDirection: Depends on adapter-utils; provider secret placeholders are resolved server-side into configuration shipped to local or remote execution.
units.keyDataModels: Provider/model, thinking level, session/cwd, models.json/provider config, skill snapshot and execution result.
units.lifecycle: Probe pinned npm CLI → discover/validate model → materialize provider config/skills → execute/resume → parse → restore.
units.testAssessment: Four tests cover remote execution, models, parser and runtime config; cleanup, cancellation and secret residue need stronger tests.
units.designRationale: Expose Pi's multi-provider tool runtime through the same adapter surface.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs provider-neutral model routing while keeping credentials inside the execution plane.
units.companyOsFit: Pinned installer is better than remote script, but direct provider config materialization stays an adapter implementation detail.
units.responsibilityConflict: All tools are enabled by default; Company OS capability leases and data egress policy must constrain the actual tool set per work action.

units.function: Postgres persistence package with 110+ table definitions, 210 tracked SQL migration files at the pin, external/embedded runtime selection, migration inspection/reconciliation, seed, backup and restore.
units.dependencyDirection: Depends on shared DTO vocabulary, Drizzle, postgres.js and patched embedded Postgres. Server and CLI import concrete tables and `Db`, so schema types penetrate service code.
units.keyDataModels: Companies, memberships, Agents, issues/goals/runs, workspaces, approvals, budgets/costs, documents/decisions, Secrets, tools, plugins, environments, routines, pipelines and audit/activity tables. Tool access alone defines over twenty related tables.
units.lifecycle: Resolve database target → bootstrap external or embedded Postgres → inspect/reconcile migration journal → apply ordered SQL → serve transactional tables → backup via pg_dump or JS stream → retain/restore with sanitization.
units.testAssessment: 24 tests cover client options, embedded startup, backup, migration safety and selected high-risk schema migrations. The migration corpus and many schemas have only targeted or integration-level coverage; restore compatibility across every historical release is not exhaustively proven.
units.designRationale: Support a low-friction local install and a serious Postgres deployment while accumulating product features through explicit migrations.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs independent schemas, migration safety, tenant isolation, backup/restore, offline/self-hosted bootstrap, audit retention and extension storage.
units.companyOsFit: Operational patterns are valuable, but the schema is Paperclip's product and cannot be copied. Company OS should use bounded schemas/modules and an outbox rather than direct table imports across all services.
units.responsibilityConflict: Generic approval payload and Agent-to-Agent hierarchy cannot enforce Company OS responsibility. Activity logging is separate from immutable responsibility/evidence state, and local-trusted bootstrap must not weaken production identity.

units.function: MCP server for reading and mutating Google Sheets through service-account credentials over stdio or HTTP.
units.dependencyDirection: Depends directly on Google APIs, MCP SDK and Zod; credential JSON/path and HTTP auth are resolved at the process boundary.
units.keyDataModels: Service-account configuration, spreadsheet/range requests, tool responses, HTTP auth config and secret-redaction values.
units.lifecycle: Load/validate credentials → construct Google client → register Sheets tools → receive stdio/HTTP call → execute external API → redact and return result.
units.testAssessment: Five tests cover config, Google client, tools and HTTP server. They are fixture/mocked tests and do not prove enterprise domain allowlists, row-level data contracts, DLP or Google audit reconciliation.
units.designRationale: Provide a concrete external data/tool integration with both local and hosted transports.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs company data connectors, authorization contracts, egress firewall checks, credential leasing and evidence of external reads/writes.
units.companyOsFit: Useful threat-model input, but a standalone MCP credential/config model is insufficient for Company OS data governance.
units.responsibilityConflict: Spreadsheet writes can be business actions. They require data-scope authorization, output classification, exact action approval when risky and immutable evidence, not merely possession of a service account.

units.function: Deterministic in-memory key/value MCP fixture with stdio startup and basic tools.
units.dependencyDirection: Depends only on MCP SDK and Zod; no Paperclip server or production store.
units.keyDataModels: In-memory key/value entries and MCP tool request/response.
units.lifecycle: Start process → register get/set/list/delete-like fixture tools → mutate process memory → discard state on exit.
units.testAssessment: Three tests cover store/tool/server behavior; it is intentionally not persistence, tenancy or security evidence.
units.designRationale: Provide a small deterministic MCP target for integration and smoke tests.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS Demo and Connector conformance tests need credential-free deterministic external-system fixtures.
units.companyOsFit: The pattern fits, but it must be labeled fixture/Demo and isolated from formal data or Agent claims.
units.responsibilityConflict: Fixture writes must never be projected as real enterprise actions or evidence.

units.function: Stdio MCP façade over Paperclip REST APIs, exposing Agent/company/task/goal/approval/document/workspace runtime read and mutation tools.
units.dependencyDirection: Depends on MCP SDK, shared schemas and Zod; reads API URL/token/company/Agent/run identity from environment and delegates authorization to the server.
units.keyDataModels: MCP tool definition, API client config, company/Agent defaults, issue/goal/approval IDs and formatted text/error responses.
units.lifecycle: Read environment credential/context → register dozens of tools → validate input → call REST endpoint → format result/error over stdio.
units.testAssessment: Only one tools test covers a broad mutable surface; API/schema drift, permission denial, cross-tenant identifiers, idempotency and destructive tool semantics need much stronger contract coverage.
units.designRationale: Give coding Agents a standard tool protocol without embedding REST details into every Agent prompt/runtime.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs a Data/Tool Connector boundary and safe Agent-facing control tools.
units.companyOsFit: MCP can be one adapter, never the core Connector contract. Company OS tools must be generated from owned API contracts and expose stable machine errors.
units.responsibilityConflict: The same token surface can create/patch/checkout work, request approvals and control runtime services. Company OS must attenuate each call to an exact capability lease, risk policy and accountable-human contract.

units.function: Minimal authoring fixture proving a manifest, capability declarations, event subscription, scoped plugin state, a health/data/action bridge and one dashboard slot.
units.dependencyDirection: Example worker and UI depend on the Paperclip Plugin SDK and host bridge; the host does not depend on example internals.
units.keyDataModels: Plugin manifest v1, issue.created event, issue-scoped state key and health/action response. It owns no durable business model.
units.lifecycle: Install/build → host validates manifest and starts worker → setup registers event/data/action handlers → issue event writes state → host probes health → uninstall removes the fixture.
units.testAssessment: Two focused tests cover manifest capabilities and event/state behavior. They are appropriate smoke coverage but do not test install, upgrade, isolation, failure recovery or UI behavior.
units.designRationale: Give plugin authors the smallest executable contract test instead of requiring them to understand the full host.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs a tiny Connector/plugin authoring smoke fixture and compatibility test that third parties can run without production credentials.
units.companyOsFit: The executable contract-test pattern fits, but Company OS must use its own Connector/extension API and deterministic fixture vocabulary.
units.responsibilityConflict: The sample only observes issue creation and cannot authorize execution, so it does not model accountable humans or responsibility contracts; it must never be presented as a real Agent.

units.function: Example project file browser/editor and comment-file-link UI backed by direct host filesystem reads and writes.
units.dependencyDirection: Worker depends on Plugin SDK project/comment APIs but directly imports node:fs/path, bypassing a mediated filesystem capability; UI depends on Paperclip slot and bridge contracts.
units.keyDataModels: Project workspace path, directory entry, file content and comment-derived path token. Files remain owned by the host filesystem rather than a plugin data store.
units.lifecycle: Read workspace path from host → resolve lexical child path → list/read/write local files → render project tabs/comment actions. It defines no revision, locking, atomic write, rollback or deletion lifecycle.
units.testAssessment: No tests across 1,114 source lines. Traversal is checked lexically, but read/write follow symlinks because paths are not realpath-verified or opened no-follow; an in-workspace symlink can expose or overwrite an external file.
units.designRationale: Demonstrate several UI extension slots with an immediately understandable local-workspace feature.
units.companyOsProblem: An Agent Boss may need evidence/artifact browsing, but production access must be capability-mediated, authorized, size-limited, auditable and safe against symlinks and races.
units.companyOsFit: The UI-slot illustration is understandable; the filesystem implementation is unacceptable for Company OS security and self-hosted enterprise boundaries.
units.responsibilityConflict: A plugin can mutate files without a declared filesystem-write capability, approval binding, actor/evidence record or responsibility contract, allowing unaccountable external effects.

units.function: Small UI-only dashboard-widget example with a worker health probe.
units.dependencyDirection: Example manifest/worker/UI depend only on the Paperclip Plugin SDK and UI host slot.
units.keyDataModels: Manifest v1, dashboardWidget slot and health result; no business or persistent data.
units.lifecycle: Install/build → register widget → start health-only worker → render static widget → uninstall.
units.testAssessment: No tests, though the entire package is only 85 TypeScript/build-source lines. It demonstrates shape, not compatibility assurance.
units.designRationale: Minimize the first successful plugin authoring experience.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS extension authors need a minimal independently buildable UI extension example.
units.companyOsFit: The small-example principle fits, while Paperclip slots, branding and runtime types do not.
units.responsibilityConflict: None directly; the static widget must remain a fixture and cannot imply execution or responsibility.

units.function: Broad development-only demonstrator for host read/write APIs, Agents/sessions, events, jobs, webhooks, HTTP, Secrets, tools, workspace access, local processes, telemetry and many UI slots.
units.dependencyDirection: Manifest and worker depend on nearly the entire Paperclip Plugin SDK surface; worker also imports unrestricted Node child_process and filesystem primitives, so capability declarations do not confine OS access.
units.keyDataModels: Instance/company config, plugin state, jobs, webhook events, tools, recent in-memory records, launcher registrations, workspace scratch files and child-process results.
units.lifecycle: Install → register broad handlers/surfaces → receive events/jobs/webhooks/actions → optionally resolve secret refs, call outbound HTTP and spawn curated host processes → keep some volatile diagnostics until worker restart.
units.testAssessment: No tests across 4,347 source lines. Allow-listed commands and disabled-by-default process demos reduce accidents, but the README itself limits local process demos to trusted development environments.
units.designRationale: Keep one executable showcase of every extension surface so host and plugin authors can discover contract breadth.
units.companyOsProblem: A compatibility lab needs coverage of the entire extension API, including negative permission cases and host-version drift.
units.companyOsFit: Useful only as a development conformance fixture. Company OS must split fixtures by capability, test denial, and execute untrusted extensions outside the host process.
units.responsibilityConflict: A single plugin can pause/resume/invoke Agents, create work, read Secrets, call HTTP and spawn local processes without a Company OS human approval and responsibility envelope. That aggregation violates least privilege for production.

units.function: Orchestration-grade smoke fixture for plugin database migrations, scoped API routes, issue creation/relations/documents/subtree summaries and idempotent wakeup.
units.dependencyDirection: Plugin owns a namespaced table but reads selected public Paperclip tables and calls host issue/orchestration APIs; UI and route contracts remain Paperclip-specific.
units.keyDataModels: Namespaced smoke_runs row linking root/child/blocker issues, billing code and JSON summary; Paperclip issues/documents/relations remain host-owned.
units.lifecycle: Migrate namespace → authenticated board-or-agent route creates resolved blocker and child → writes relation/document → requests idempotent wakeup → stores summary → query route joins plugin and core data.
units.testAssessment: Three focused tests cover manifest/database/route shape, orchestration path and route dispatch. It does not cover migration rollback, concurrent duplicate requests, uninstall retention, authorization denial or failure compensation after partial writes.
units.designRationale: Exercise realistic cross-surface orchestration in a small package rather than relying on unit mocks of each host API.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs compatibility fixtures proving extension migrations, actor propagation, idempotency and orchestration projections across upgrades.
units.companyOsFit: The smoke-test strategy fits. Company OS must add a human principal, responsibility contract, exact approval/action digest and compensation assertions before issuing executable work.
units.responsibilityConflict: The board-or-agent route can create and wake Agent work with an optional Agent/user actor but no mandatory accountable human or responsibility contract.

units.function: Paperclip environment-driver plugin that delegates Cloudflare Sandbox lifecycle and command execution to a separately deployed authenticated bridge.
units.dependencyDirection: Plugin depends on Paperclip Plugin SDK contracts and a custom HTTP/SSE bridge protocol; Cloudflare SDK/runtime is isolated in the bridge template.
units.keyDataModels: Secret-ref bridge token, endpoint/API prefix, keep-alive/sleep/reuse/session options, opaque provider lease ID, sentinel metadata and normalized execute result.
units.lifecycle: Validate configuration and bridge health, acquire/resume lease through bridge, prepare workspace/sentinel, execute with bounded HTTP timeout and optional SSE, then release or destroy.
units.testAssessment: 31 tests across six files cover configuration, bridge HTTP errors/timeouts, lifecycle, streaming, command forwarding and metadata. They mock the bridge and do not prove Cloudflare network isolation, bridge deployment security, retry/idempotency under ambiguous HTTP failure, or real provider cleanup.
units.designRationale: Keep vendor SDK and edge-runtime requirements outside the host process while exposing one environment-driver contract.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs provider-neutral local/remote execution nodes without placing vendor credentials or private sessions in its control plane.
units.companyOsFit: The narrow bridge and secret-ref pattern are useful. Company OS should own a versioned execution-node protocol with idempotency keys, authenticated workload identity, structured stable error codes, health/attestation and reconciliation rather than inherit Paperclip's endpoint and lease vocabulary.
units.responsibilityConflict: The bridge authenticates a bearer token but does not bind commands to an approved action, data grant, accountable human or runtime proof. That binding belongs above the provider adapter.

units.function: Deployable Cloudflare Worker/Durable Object bridge implementing health, probe, lease acquire/resume/release/destroy and command execution endpoints.
units.dependencyDirection: Bridge depends directly on @cloudflare/sandbox; Paperclip reaches it only through HTTP/SSE. No Company OS-neutral protocol package exists.
units.keyDataModels: Bearer-authenticated JSON requests, provider lease/sandbox IDs, named/default sessions, sentinel file, timeout/result envelope and SSE stdout/stderr/complete events.
units.lifecycle: Constant-time bearer verification, resolve/create sandbox and session, ensure workspace, write/verify sentinel, stage stdin, run quoted login-shell command, clean timed-out sessions and temporary files, then keep alive or destroy.
units.testAssessment: 16 tests cover auth, ID helpers, session-scoped sentinel operations, quoting/env validation, stdin cleanup, SSE and timeout-shaped behavior. There are no authorization-scope tests, replay/idempotency tests, rate limits, schema validation/fuzzing, audit correlation, provider integration, or reconciliation after partial failure.
units.designRationale: Bridge edge-only provider APIs behind a small service boundary and avoid loading Cloudflare-specific code into the main server.
units.companyOsProblem: A customer-local execution node or vendor bridge needs a small, replaceable protocol and reliable lease lifecycle.
units.companyOsFit: Separation and constant-time secret comparison are useful. Company OS needs signed short-lived workload tokens, request/version/schema validation, idempotency, cancellation, capability/attestation and action/evidence correlation; generic 500 responses must not leak raw internal messages.
units.responsibilityConflict: A static bridge token authorizes all operations and carries no principal/action scope. It cannot itself prove a human-approved responsibility chain.

units.function: Daytona-backed environment driver with image/snapshot creation, native file sync, command streaming/polling, reusable stop/start leases, sentinels and cleanup recovery.
units.dependencyDirection: Plugin depends on Paperclip Plugin SDK and exact @daytonaio/sdk 0.203.0; Daytona credentials are resolved through secret-ref/environment configuration.
units.keyDataModels: API endpoint/key, image-or-snapshot choice, workspace/timeouts/auto-delete/reuse, opaque sandbox ID, lease metadata, file manifest and command result.
units.lifecycle: Validate mutually exclusive image/snapshot, create or start sandbox, verify/write sentinel, sync files, execute and stream/poll, stop reusable leases or delete ephemeral ones, and delete on fatal preparation failures.
units.testAssessment: 131 focused tests in one large test file cover validation, lifecycle, sentinel recovery, command/streaming behavior, path canonicalization, symlinks, binary/file sync, cleanup and SDK edge cases. The suite is mock-heavy; no real-provider integration or concurrency/reconciliation proof exists. Documentation still promises an advisory bubblewrap wrapper that current source explicitly removed.
units.designRationale: Map a rich provider SDK behind the shared environment-driver lifecycle while exploiting native stop/start and file APIs.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs robust provider adapters, workspace transfer and cleanup without allowing provider types or credentials into core/application.
units.companyOsFit: Lifecycle failure handling, sentinel ownership, file canonicalization and exact SDK pinning are strong references. The implementation is vendor/Paperclip coupled and its documentation drift shows that isolation claims require executable compatibility evidence.
units.responsibilityConflict: A valid lease executes arbitrary commands without an action/approval/data-grant binding. Company OS must classify and authorize before dispatch and record exact runtime/image/permission attestation afterward.

units.function: Thin E2B environment driver for template-based sandbox creation, command execution, timeout extension, reuse and kill.
units.dependencyDirection: Plugin depends on Paperclip Plugin SDK and e2b ^2.19.0; E2B API key is a secret-ref or environment fallback.
units.keyDataModels: API key, template, workdir, timeout/reuse settings, sandbox ID, shell metadata and normalized execution output.
units.lifecycle: Create or reconnect by sandbox ID, set timeout, ensure workspace, execute shell command with stdin/env/cwd, retain reusable lease or kill it.
units.testAssessment: 19 tests cover validation, acquire/resume/release/destroy, timeout, command construction and errors. Coverage is appropriate for a thin adapter but lacks real provider, network/isolation, concurrent reuse, ambiguous failure and cleanup reconciliation tests.
units.designRationale: Expose E2B as another installable implementation of one environment-driver contract with minimal local policy.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS may offer optional vendor execution connectors while preserving runtime neutrality.
units.companyOsFit: Provider lifecycle mapping is a useful reference, but the code offers little differentiated infrastructure and remains coupled to Paperclip contracts and a floating compatible SDK range.
units.responsibilityConflict: No human responsibility or exact permission/evidence binding exists at this layer; it must remain a subordinate execution adapter.

units.function: exe.dev remote-VM environment driver using the provider HTTPS API for VM lifecycle and SSH for setup, file transfer and command execution.
units.dependencyDirection: Plugin depends on Paperclip Plugin SDK plus host ssh/scp/ssh-agent/key files and exe.dev HTTPS endpoints; it has no provider SDK dependency.
units.keyDataModels: API key/base URL, region/image, SSH user/key/agent, setup command, workdir/timeouts/reuse, VM name/address and lease metadata.
units.lifecycle: Create VM via API, wait for SSH, optionally install runtime with a default remote setup command, create sentinel, execute/sync through SSH, retain a reusable live VM or delete it; probe can create and delete a billed VM.
units.testAssessment: 35 mocked tests cover config, API lifecycle, SSH argv/quoting, key/agent auth, setup, streaming and cleanup. They do not prove host-key trust, provider behavior, network policy, VM isolation, cost containment, concurrent reuse or recovery from an unknown create/delete outcome.
units.designRationale: Use ubiquitous HTTPS and SSH instead of a proprietary SDK, allowing the provider to remain a standalone installable plugin.
units.companyOsProblem: Self-hosted/local enterprise deployments may need SSH-based execution nodes, but they must be governed and safely enrolled.
units.companyOsFit: Argument-array discipline and transport separation are worth studying. Direct host key paths/ssh-agent fallback, remote bootstrap scripts, always-live reuse and a paid probe are unsafe defaults for Company OS. A local node should use explicit enrollment, pinned host identity, prepared images and cost/network policy.
units.responsibilityConflict: Possession of host SSH credentials effectively grants broad machine authority without responsibility-contract scope. Company OS must not treat transport access as organizational authorization.

units.function: Kubernetes execution provider with per-company namespaces, quotas, restricted pod policy, deny-all networking, scoped egress, image allowlists, per-run secrets, alpha agent-sandbox CR and batch Job backends.
units.dependencyDirection: Plugin depends on Paperclip Plugin SDK, @kubernetes/client-node ^1.0.0 and zod. A SandboxOrchestrator interface separates alpha agents.x-k8s.io/v1alpha1 and stable batch/v1 backends.
units.keyDataModels: Validated cluster/provider config, tenant namespace/resources, image policy, egress grant, workload/secret owner references, opaque lease metadata, backend capability, command/file-sync result and cleanup state.
units.lifecycle: Validate config/image/network grants, ensure tenant namespace/service account/quota/restricted policies, create workload and scoped egress, create owner-bound secret, wait for pod, exec/sync when supported, then release or forcibly reconcile every resource.
units.testAssessment: 195 tests across 21 files cover manifest/config, image allowlist, namespace/RBAC/quota, NetworkPolicy/Cilium, pod/CR/job manifests, secret ownership, lease cleanup, upload interception, readiness, execution and multiple failure paths. It is the strongest provider suite reviewed, but provider integration is manual smoke testing; the default CRD is alpha and Job mode cannot support multi-command adapter installation.
units.designRationale: Use Kubernetes-native tenant and workload boundaries, with a swap interface for evolving sandbox backends and defensive cleanup independent of owner-reference success.
units.companyOsProblem: Self-hosted enterprise needs enforceable tenant isolation, image/data-egress policy, secret lifetime, resource quotas and recoverable local execution.
units.companyOsFit: Tenant orchestration, image allowlist, owner-bound secrets, deny-all baseline, per-work scoped egress and force cleanup are strong patterns. Company OS must define its own execution/data-authorization contracts, fail closed when exact FQDN enforcement is required, pin/attest images, and not make an alpha CRD canonical. Source correctly disables service-account token automount despite stale README text.
units.responsibilityConflict: Infrastructure isolation does not decide whether a human authorized the action or data egress. Every workload must carry an opaque responsibility/action digest and produce secret-free runtime proof; broad standard-NetworkPolicy public egress cannot satisfy an exact data contract.

units.function: Modal environment driver for registry-image sandboxes, optional network blocking, command/file execution and detach-based lease reuse.
units.dependencyDirection: Plugin depends on Paperclip Plugin SDK and Modal client APIs; token ID/secret are stored as secret-ref configuration.
units.keyDataModels: Token pair, environment/image/workdir/timeouts, blockNetwork/reuse flags, Modal sandbox ID, tags, shell metadata and normalized command result.
units.lifecycle: Authenticate, resolve registry image, create or reconnect sandbox, ensure workspace, execute and stage stdin, detach a reusable lease or terminate it.
units.testAssessment: 26 mocked tests cover authentication, validation, create/resume/detach/terminate, command quoting, stdin and timeout behavior. They do not prove provider network blocking, image provenance, concurrent detach/reconnect, maximum lifetime or cleanup reconciliation.
units.designRationale: Exploit Modal's image and sandbox primitives while translating detach semantics into the shared lease contract.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs explicit capability negotiation because providers differ on pause, detach, network and persistence semantics.
units.companyOsFit: The honest distinction between detach and pause plus optional network blocking is a useful lifecycle reference. The adapter is otherwise vendor/Paperclip specific and should not be copied wholesale.
units.responsibilityConflict: Network blocking is configuration rather than a responsibility/data authorization proof, and detach extends the lifetime of credentials/workspace. Company OS must record retention and accountable approval separately.

units.function: Thin Novita Agent Sandbox driver with template creation, command execution, auto-pause, pause/resume reuse and kill.
units.dependencyDirection: Plugin depends on Paperclip Plugin SDK and novita-sandbox ^1.0.3-b2; API key is resolved through secret-ref or environment fallback.
units.keyDataModels: API key, template, workdir, request/sandbox timeouts, beta auto-pause/reuse flags, sandbox ID and shell/result metadata.
units.lifecycle: Create from template or reconnect, set timeout, detect shell, ensure workspace, execute, pause reusable lease or kill it.
units.testAssessment: Eight mocked tests cover the main lifecycle and execution path. There is insufficient coverage for beta SDK drift, command quoting/adversarial inputs, ambiguous failures, concurrency, cleanup, network/isolation or real provider behavior.
units.designRationale: Offer the provider through the same environment-driver surface with minimal policy and optional reuse.
units.companyOsProblem: Connector capability declarations must distinguish provider-specific preview/beta lifecycle behavior.
units.companyOsFit: Pause/resume capability vocabulary is useful, but the adapter is thin, beta-dependent and under-tested. It should be an optional future connector after its SDK and semantics mature.
units.responsibilityConflict: Pausing preserves state and potentially sensitive data without a retention contract or accountable approval; provider lifecycle alone cannot supply that governance.

units.function: Cross-provider sandbox image/runtime requirements and capability matrix for Paperclip's first-party providers.
units.dependencyDirection: Documentation describes assumptions imposed on external images, provider APIs and the Paperclip environment driver contract; no code depends on it mechanically.
units.keyDataModels: Provider capability matrix, image prerequisites, command/file-sync constraints, lease reuse semantics and advisory isolation notes.
units.lifecycle: Operator supplies image/provider configuration, plugin probes prerequisites, lease executes, and release either pauses/stops/detaches or destroys according to provider semantics.
units.testAssessment: No executable conformance test binds this document to providers. It currently says Daytona degrades to plain execution when bubblewrap is absent, while Daytona source and DIRECTORY-CONSTRAINT-FINDINGS say the wrapper was removed entirely. It also says Kubernetes workloads automount a service-account token, while both current pod builders set automountServiceAccountToken=false.
units.designRationale: Centralize provider-specific prerequisites so images are prebuilt and runtime execution avoids expensive setup.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs a machine-verifiable execution-profile contract covering isolation, image provenance, network policy, secrets, lifecycle, capabilities and runtime attestation.
units.companyOsFit: The matrix format and immutable-image principle are useful, but prose that drifts from code cannot be the trust source. Required confinement must fail closed and be demonstrated by compatibility tests and short-lived secret-free attestations.
units.responsibilityConflict: Calling isolation advisory while continuing execution obscures who accepted the risk. Company OS must surface the effective trust tier and bind any exception to an accountable human and exact policy digest.

units.function: CLI scaffolder for a Paperclip plugin package and its worker/manifest/UI entrypoints.
units.dependencyDirection: Depends on the Plugin SDK and emits packages coupled to its v1 manifest/build layout.
units.keyDataModels: Template package metadata and entrypoint paths, not business data.
units.lifecycle: Prompt/arguments → create files → install/build against SDK → plugin is later installed by the host.
units.testAssessment: One entrypoint test checks generated structure; it does not validate production distribution, signing or sandboxing.
units.designRationale: Reduce authoring errors and make the preferred extension shape easy to start.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS will need a Connector/extension starter with conformance and provenance defaults.
units.companyOsFit: The scaffolding idea fits, but emitted Paperclip manifest/types and branding do not.
units.responsibilityConflict: Generated templates should default to no capabilities and require explicit human-reviewed grants.

units.function: Deterministic local fake sandbox provider that exercises environment-driver leases, setup sessions, templates and command execution without external infrastructure.
units.dependencyDirection: Implements Plugin SDK environment-driver contracts and writes only to temporary local directories.
units.keyDataModels: Fake lease ID, environment/session ID, template reference, redacted connection metadata and deterministic driver config.
units.lifecycle: Validate/probe → allocate temp lease → execute/sync → release or retain → capture template/setup → clean up.
units.testAssessment: One focused test covers the integrated provider lifecycle. It is intentionally not a security sandbox and should not be used as production proof.
units.designRationale: Make provider-plugin integration deterministic and credential-free in CI.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs a deterministic Connector/execution-node conformance fixture that is never represented as a real Agent or sandbox.
units.companyOsFit: Strong testing pattern; Company OS should build its own neutral fixture against its Connector SDK.
units.responsibilityConflict: Fixture actions must remain Demo/test-only and must not mint formal identity, credentials or responsibility records.

units.function: Large first-party knowledge plugin that captures sources, maintains file-backed multi-space wikis, distills Paperclip work into cited pages, runs Agent-backed queries/maintenance and exposes API/tools/UI.
units.dependencyDirection: Plugin owns namespaced relational metadata and local wiki files but consumes broad Paperclip issue/comment/document/event/Agent/session/routine/skill APIs and UI slots; it is not a neutral knowledge service.
units.keyDataModels: Wiki/space/source/page bindings, operation and distillation cursors/snapshots, source windows, generated patch proposals, managed Agent/routine/skill bindings and file hash/provenance records across three SQL migrations.
units.lifecycle: Bootstrap files/schema → capture manual or Paperclip sources → debounce/cursor source windows → redact secret-like material → create visible operation work → generate cited review patches → verify hashes/policy → approve or conditionally auto-apply → advance cursor only on success → lint/archive/repair spaces.
units.testAssessment: 101 tests across 20,193 source lines cover schema/surfaces, UI, event isolation, cursor success rules, provenance, secret suppression, bounded backfill, review patches, authenticated-public auto-apply refusal, stale hashes, size limits, protected files and Agent sessions. Remaining risk is the very large single plugin/worker, Paperclip-specific integration breadth and limited real database/filesystem/concurrency E2E evidence.
units.designRationale: Keep optional knowledge behavior outside core while making source provenance, generated changes and maintenance visible as ordinary work.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs governed institutional knowledge, original-source evidence, FDE template learning and safe improvement proposals without storing private reasoning as control-plane truth.
units.companyOsFit: Cursor-after-success, source-window provenance, redaction, stale-hash checks and review-before-write are strong patterns. Company OS should separate knowledge authorization, evidence, generated proposals and execution, and avoid Paperclip issue/Agent/UI coupling.
units.responsibilityConflict: Default auto-apply can be allowed in trusted local modes, while Company OS must bind any consequential knowledge/policy mutation to a classified action, exact digest and accountable human approval. LLM synthesis is evidence-derived content, not authoritative responsibility proof.

units.function: Read-only workspace change projection that computes bounded Git staged/unstaged/untracked or base-ref diffs and renders them in workspace tabs.
units.dependencyDirection: Core diff service depends on Node filesystem/child_process and small Paperclip workspace metadata types; worker/UI adapt it to Plugin SDK and @pierre/diffs.
units.keyDataModels: Validated diff query, file status/patch/warning, byte/file caps, workspace metadata and summarized statistics. It does not persist a separate database.
units.lifecycle: Resolve and realpath workspace/repo → normalize filters/base ref → invoke git with argument arrays/timeouts/buffers → realpath/no-follow untracked files → cap patches and aggregate warnings → validate bridge response → render; no mutation occurs.
units.testAssessment: 26 tests across 2,999 source lines cover contracts, UI model/error state, staged/unstaged/rename/delete/untracked/binary/oversized data, caps, filters, base refs and external-symlink non-disclosure. TOCTOU remains possible between realpath and open on hostile filesystems, and real Git/plugin integration is local-only rather than sandbox-attested.
units.designRationale: Keep expensive and security-sensitive filesystem/Git computation in a plugin-local service with strict output bounds rather than the browser.
units.companyOsProblem: Evidence review needs safe bounded workspace/artifact change projections without importing an Agent vendor session or exposing arbitrary host files.
units.companyOsFit: The service shape, execFile argument discipline, realpath/no-follow checks, structured warnings and caps are strong. Company OS should place it behind an evidence/artifact reader port and execution-node attestation rather than a trusted Web plugin.
units.responsibilityConflict: Read-only projection does not approve or publish changes. Company OS must bind the resulting digest and source workspace/run to the responsibility record before a human approves publication.

units.function: Official worker/UI/testing/build SDK with versioned JSON-RPC, manifest and lifecycle types, capability-gated host clients, events, jobs, tools, state/entities, local folders, Secrets, Agent sessions and same-origin React slots.
units.dependencyDirection: Depends on shared and Zod with React as peer. Plugins compile against it; the server implements the host side and the UI loads SDK-compatible bundles.
units.keyDataModels: Plugin manifest v1, JSON-RPC request/result/error, invocation metadata, domain event, job, tool, state scope, entity, UI slot/host context, environment driver and Agent session.
units.lifecycle: Validate manifest/version → install package → start worker process → setup registrations → capability-check worker↔host RPC → deliver events/jobs/API/tool calls → health/config changes → bounded shutdown. UI bundles load separately in the browser.
units.testAssessment: Six SDK tests cover host client, worker host, protocol/UI/testing paths, plus extensive server tests. The README explicitly calls deployment early: workers and UI are trusted, dynamic install assumes single-node writable filesystem/npm/network, and multi-instance artifact distribution is unresolved.
units.designRationale: Provide one discoverable extension API while keeping persistence, auth and core mutations behind host services.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs version negotiation, capability declarations, extension isolation, durable event delivery, package provenance, multi-node distribution and separate Connector versus UI-extension trust models.
units.companyOsFit: Fail-closed operations, manifest validation and host-mediated resources fit. The API is Paperclip-domain-wide, same-origin UI is not isolated, and resolved secrets can cross into a trusted worker; Company OS needs a narrower capability/lease protocol.
units.responsibilityConflict: Plugins can create/update work, invoke Agents and respond to approvals through broad capabilities. Company OS must require accountable-human sponsorship and exact action authorization, not merely a manifest capability.

units.function: Cross-runtime public vocabulary for server, UI, CLI, adapters and plugins: constants, DTO types, Zod input validators, API paths, portability, feature/app definitions and presentation helpers.
units.dependencyDirection: Nearly every workspace depends inward on this package; it depends mainly on Zod. A 2,300+ line barrel and 1,400+ line constants file make it both contract layer and product-wide coupling hub.
units.keyDataModels: Company, Agent, issue, goal, run, approval, budget, secret, tool, plugin, environment, decision, document, artifact, project, membership and live-event DTOs plus their enums/validators.
units.lifecycle: Request input is parsed into shared DTOs, persisted through separate DB schema, returned to UI/plugins and sometimes serialized for company portability. Generated app and telemetry files are regenerated from source catalogs.
units.testAssessment: 51 tests cover 15 validator groups and many focused helpers. Many pure type files and the enormous enum/barrel surface have indirect compile-time coverage only; server and UI can therefore become lockstep coupled.
units.designRationale: Prevent duplicated request/response shapes across a TypeScript monorepo and make provider adapters share product terminology.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS also needs stable wire contracts, validators, portable IDs and machine error codes across Web, API, Connector and deployments.
units.companyOsFit: The schema-first approach fits, but Company OS must separate domain value objects, public API DTOs, Connector wire types and UI copy instead of one universal shared package.
units.responsibilityConflict: Several enums expose `require_approval`, risk and principal concepts without enforcing exact action/contract/human/evidence bindings; shared labels and English denial messages must not become authority contracts.

units.function: Builds and validates a catalog of bundled/optional Agent skills, files, assets, sources, trust levels and compatibility metadata.
units.dependencyDirection: Depends on shared frontmatter/schema helpers; generated manifest is consumed by server/UI and release packaging.
units.keyDataModels: CatalogSkill, source reference, file kind, trust level (`markdown_only`, `assets`, `scripts_executables`), compatibility and generated manifest.
units.lifecycle: Scan catalog files → parse frontmatter → validate slugs/source/file graph → hash/package metadata → compare or write deterministic generated manifest → ship catalog.
units.testAssessment: Five tests cover builder, frontmatter, packaged artifacts, release-content contracts and shipped manifest. Runtime skill execution safety remains outside the catalog package.
units.designRationale: Make instructional and executable Agent assets discoverable and release-verifiable with explicit trust classification.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS FDE templates and later training need versioned, provenance-aware capabilities with trust and compatibility metadata.
units.companyOsFit: Trust-tier and deterministic manifest ideas are valuable; Paperclip skills/content/brand should not be copied wholesale.
units.responsibilityConflict: A skill is guidance or executable material, not authority. Installation and use must be bounded by Agent role, data scope, human owner and signed version.

units.function: Builds and validates deployable team templates containing Agents, projects, tasks, local/external skills and environment inputs.
units.dependencyDirection: Reads the skills catalog generated manifest and team markdown/frontmatter; generated team manifest is consumed by product onboarding/import paths.
units.keyDataModels: CatalogTeam schema `agentcompanies/v1`, Agent/project/task graph, reportsTo/owner/assignee references, skill requirements, source refs and secret/plain environment inputs.
units.lifecycle: Scan team bundle → parse entity files → validate graph and referenced skills → summarize env inputs/trust → write deterministic catalog manifest → import into a company.
units.testAssessment: Two tests cover builder and shipped catalog. Human roles, responsibility contracts, approval policies, data contracts, template upgrades and rollback are not represented or tested.
units.designRationale: Turn a repeatable Agent organization and workflow into a distributable onboarding artifact.
units.companyOsProblem: This directly anticipates Company OS FDE industry templates, implementation repeatability and template provenance.
units.companyOsFit: The catalog pipeline is a strong reference, but Company OS templates must include humans, departments, accountable roles, responsibility contracts, data authorization, risk/approval policies and migration versions.
units.responsibilityConflict: Current reporting/ownership references are Agent-centric. Importing them as formal organization state would omit accountable humans and may silently grant tools/secrets.
